**Result: the value is 1, for every x with tan x > 0 (i.e. x ∈ (0, π/2) mod π).**

**Domain.** The second integrand 1/(t(1+t²)) is singular at t = 0. The integral from 1/e to cot x is therefore defined only if cot x > 0. Since tan x = 1/cot x, this is the same as tan x > 0.

**Substitution.** In the second integral put t = 1/u, so dt = −du/u².

The integrand becomes

1/(t(1+t²)) · dt = u/(1+1/u²) · (−du/u²) = −u/(1+u²) du.

The limits change as follows: t = 1/e gives u = e, and t = cot x gives u = tan x. Hence

∫_{1/e}^{cot x} dt/(t(1+t²)) = −∫_e^{tan x} u/(1+u²) du = ∫_{tan x}^{e} u/(1+u²) du.

**Combine.** The sum is

∫_{1/e}^{tan x} t/(1+t²) dt + ∫_{tan x}^{e} t/(1+t²) dt = ∫_{1/e}^{e} t/(1+t²) dt.

Evaluating,

∫_{1/e}^{e} t/(1+t²) dt = ½[ln(1+t²)]_{1/e}^{e} = ½ ln((1+e²)/(1+e⁻²)) = ½ ln(e²) = 1.

Here (1+e²)/(1+e⁻²) = e² because 1+e⁻² = (e²+1)/e².

Final answer: 1
